transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Aureus Lead ML Eng), Leah (Backend), Tomás (Product), Rina (SRE)
Shared artifacts: Pilot dashboard link (redwood.com/s/au-pilot-453), canonicalization doc (shared google drive link), hit-rate csv (shared)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Reviewed current KV/prefix cache hit rates (global 18% baseline, week-over-week up from 12%).
- Discussed prompt reuse patterns: session affinity, canonicalization, templated prompts causing low reuse.
- Proposed experiments: prefix canonicalization, prefetch heavy-list queries, TTL bump for stable sessions, 24h production replay.
- Action items: Redwood to send config snippets; Aureus to share logs; schedule dedicated benchmark if improvements not observed.

TOPICS:
- Metrics recap and anomalies
- Prompt normalization / canonicalization rules
- Prefetch strategy and TTL tuning
- Routing/orchestration impacts (region + dedicated fallback)
- Next steps and ownership

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone, thanks for jumping on for the weekly sync, um let's do a quick run through of numbers and then go into the tuning ideas. Jordan, do you want to start with any updates on your side?
[00:12] Jordan Meyers: yeah thanks Maya, quick update — we ran the prefix-only patch last night on staging, saw a small bump, like 15 to 18 percent hit, so moving in right direction but not — not where we'd hoped. there's also some noisy traffic from our search ingestion pipeline that skewed some of the numbers.
[00:32] Diego Ramos: cool, thanks. can you clarify whether the 18% is global across all endpoints or just the chat endpoints?
[00:40] Jordan Meyers: that's global, if you isolate the QA microservice it's more like 24, but the conversational channel is lower.
[00:48] Priya Nambiar: one quick note — the staging run didn't include canonicalization rules we discussed (i.e. strip timestamps, normalize user metadata), so I think your reuse ceiling is artificially low.
[00:58] Leah Ito: ah right that was on our backlog, we didn't want to touch production prompt shaping yet.
[01:05] Maya Chen: that's a big one — canonicalization tends to be high leverage. Diego, do you mind walking through a concrete normalization ruleset you recommend?
[01:13] Diego Ramos: sure, high level: 1) remove ephemeral tokens (timestamps, session ids), 2) map synonyms in the product domain (e.g., "order" vs "purchase"), 3) canonicalize date formats, and 4) collapse minor punctuation differences. we'll provide a small regex + deterministic replacer snippet. not perfect but will collapse a lot of variance.
[01:38] Tomás Alvarez: quick Q — will canonicalization risk changing intent? we worry about false merges where prompts that look similar but need different responses get routed to cached results.
[01:47] Priya Nambiar: we handle that by tiered caching: prefix-level for high-confidence canonical matches and a separate fallback path for low-confidence; we can tune threshold. so it's an engineering knob.
[02:00] Rina Kapoor: also want to call out session affinity — a lot of our users have long sessions with minor edits; if we increase TTL for those sessions we can get big win. current TTL 60s, maybe bump to 5 minutes for affinity scenarios.
[02:13] Maya Chen: good point. Diego, suggested prefetching approaches?
[02:16] Diego Ramos: two ideas — proactive prefetch for top-n likely next prompts based on N-gram analysis, and opportunistic prefetch on session start for templates. Prefetch is cheap if hit-rate increases justify the extra tokens; we'll show cost math.
[02:31] Jordan Meyers: we worried about token costs — prefetching could double request volume if misconfigured. need conservative prefetch policy.
[02:40] Diego Ramos: agreed, start with top-1 prefetch and conservative blacklists. and instrument cost.
[02:46] [03:00] Sam Park: quick interjection — on the console we can surface token delta per prefetch experiment so your finance folks can see projected spend. we'll attach that to the experiment.
[03:12] Jordan Meyers: perfect.
[03:15] [03:30] Leah Ito: a messy thing we saw — prompts from mobile have extra boilerplate (OS version, device id) that massively reduces reuse; would canonicalization remove that safely?
[03:42] Priya Nambiar: yes we have pattern examples to strip device metadata; Diego's snippet will include those.
[03:47] [04:00] Diego Ramos: also want to call out KV cache naming — currently some keys include dynamic session tokens; we recommend replacing with stable user or conversation id only when privacy allows. if not allowed, use hashed stable buckets.
[04:14] Jordan Meyers: privacy is strict for us, so we'll need hashing + salt with customer-managed KMS. are those integrations tested?
[04:22] Maya Chen: yes, Private and Dedicated modes support KMS integrations; we can provide a sample HSM/KMS flow. Diego will include the snippet in the doc.
[04:30] [04:45] Tomás Alvarez: curious about routing/orchestration — if cache hit-rate remains low on hosted, we might want a Dedicated fallback for predictable latency. how do we decide threshold?
[04:57] Maya Chen: typical rule is if prefix/KV uplift under canonicalization < 20% and latency variability remains high, we propose a Dedicated run for a week to validate throughput and latency SLOs. we'll do cost/benefit in the note.
[05:10] Diego Ramos: also remember that batching and KV cache interplay — larger batch windows can erode hit-rate if keys are ephemeral; we recommend workload-aware batching.
[05:20] Rina Kapoor: can you give a concrete experiment plan we can run in staging to prove improvements?
[05:26] Diego Ramos: yes: 1) baseline 48h replay with current config (we have that), 2) apply canonicalization rules + hashed key change + TTL bump to 5 minutes for affinity sessions and run 24h, 3) run prefetch top-1 on a small fraction (5%) of traffic for 24h, 4) compare hit-rate, p50/p95 latency, token spend delta. we'll provide scripts and dashboard.
[05:52] Jordan Meyers: timeline for that — we can get logs ready by Friday. we want to run the replay early next week.
[05:59] Maya Chen: great, Diego and Priya will assemble the config today and post into the shared folder.
[06:05] [06:20] Leah Ito: about eviction — what's best practice for prompt eviction heuristics? we saw some prompts get evicted too aggressively causing churn.
[06:30] Priya Nambiar: we usually recommend LRU with weighted recency for templates, and a small protected set for frequently used templates. TTL bump for protected items helps. also smarter eviction that considers token cost of regeneration.
[06:45] Tomás Alvarez: can Redwood's console expose eviction stats?
[06:49] Sam Park: yes we can add an eviction heatmap to the pilot dashboard; we'll turn that on.
[06:55] [07:10] Jordan Meyers: one odd metric — there's a spike of low reuse queries right around 03:00 UTC daily, looks like a batch process. we'll scrub and maybe exclude those from baseline.
[07:20] Diego Ramos: good call, filter those when calculating user-facing hit-rate.
[07:23] [07:40] Rina Kapoor: two quick non-technical asks: SOC2 artifacts and SSO integration docs — legal wants them by next week.
[07:50] Maya Chen: noted, we'll push the SOC2 pack and SAML implementation guide to the shared drive.
[07:56] [08:10] Tomás Alvarez: can we get a quick cost model that shows break-even hit-rate for prefetch at different token sizes?
[08:18] Maya Chen: yes, Diego will include the spreadsheet; we'll also include p50/p95 latency offsets.
[08:24] [08:40] Diego Ramos: one more thought — canonicalization introduces potential false-positives; we'll add a safety threshold and audit logs for cache hits that used canonicalized keys. you can inspect and roll back rules.
[08:54] Jordan Meyers: appreciate that.
[09:00] [09:20] Maya Chen: ok pulling together the wrap: Diego will send the config snippet and prefetch policy, Jordan will deliver logs, Rina will run staging replay, Maya will send pricing and Dedicated fallback plan. any objections?
[09:36] Leah Ito: none.
[09:38] Tomás Alvarez: sounds good.
[09:40] [09:50] Priya Nambiar: I'll also add examples of canonicalization rules (regex) and a short runbook for rolling them back.
[09:57] Maya Chen: great. we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time for results.

CLOSING SUMMARY / RECAP:
- Current hit-rate: baseline ~18% global, 24% on QA service.
- High-leverage experiments: canonicalization (regex-based), TTL bump for affinity, prefetch top-1 on 5% traffic, hashed stable keys for privacy.
- Short-term plan: customer to scrub and upload 48h logs; Redwood to supply config and cost model; run replays and small live prefetch experiment; then reassess for Dedicated.
